subject: PSHE
title: Positive friendships and relationships
outcome: Identify features of positive friendships and relationships.
credit: Lesson resource · CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: free for classroom use, share and adapt with credit, no resale
definition: A positive friendship has care and respect. People can have different likes and other friends. They listen, ask before sharing and respect a no. One kind act does not prove that every part of a friendship is safe.
flag_rule: Green flag means this action shows care or respect. Amber flag means pause, check what happened and ask for help if needed. Judge the action and its context, not a whole person. Amber never means put up with harm. If someone feels unsafe, get a trusted adult at once; do not wait to finish a sort. These two labels are learning prompts, not a safety test.

sort.text: A friend asks before sharing another person's drawing and accepts no.
sort.reason: They respect choice and the person's work.

sort.text: A friend listens when someone wants a quiet break.
sort.reason: They respect a need and give space.

sort.text: A friend is pleased that someone enjoys a different activity too.
sort.reason: They respect different likes and other choices.

sort.text: A friend keeps choosing the task without asking what the other person wants.
sort.reason: Both people need a chance to choose. Pause and ask for a fair plan.

sort.text: A friend shares a drawing after the other person has said no.
sort.reason: They ignore a clear choice. Stop the sharing and ask a trusted adult for help.

sort.text: A friend says sorry for an unkind reply but keeps doing the same thing.
sort.reason: A sorry needs a change in action. Ask a trusted adult for help if it continues or feels unsafe.

case.title: Choosing a shared activity
case.text: Two invented young people plan a quiet craft task. One asks to use a drawing. The other says no. The first person accepts this and chooses a new idea. Later one keeps choosing each next step without asking. The other wants a fair turn to choose. No names, personal details or unkind words are shown.
case.model: Accepting no is a green flag because it respects choice. Choosing every step without asking is an amber flag because both people need a say. They could pause and agree a turn each, or ask school staff to help. Judge each action; one green action does not cancel the amber concern.
case.safer_step: They could say, Can we each choose one step? If that is not respected, they can stop the task and ask trusted school staff in private.

choices.B: Make a two-part scene map. Identify one green and one amber action, give a reason for each, then suggest a respectful next step and help route.
choices.C: Write an advice note about the same scene. Explain one green and one amber action with reasons, then give a respectful next step and help route.

success: Identify care, respect or choice in an invented action.
Explain one green and one amber action using the scene.
Suggest a respectful next step and a trusted adult help route.
private_card: What a good friend does is an optional keep card for a helpful action to remember. It stays with the pupil. Use the invented scene, leave it blank or pass. No real friend, relationship, name or experience is requested. Do not collect, photograph, display, compare or copy it into evidence. An agreed scribe returns it to the pupil.
help: Ask a trusted adult or school staff in private. Use words, a note, HELP or a usual aid. Staff can take a concern to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. If one adult is unavailable or help is not enough, ask another trusted adult. For an immediate safety concern, get adult help at once. No named service, organisation, website or phone number is needed.
step_out: Before teaching, agree the discreet HELP or PAUSE signal and familiar supervised place and route. Staff acknowledge it quietly and keep adult support. No public reason is needed. Offer a neutral task, supported return or private catch-up. Do not send a learner away alone. Pass is not failure.
safeguarding: Any disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. Listen calmly, reassure, do not probe, investigate or promise secrecy. Follow urgent school procedures for immediate concerns. Keep real concerns and identifying details in the separate safeguarding record, not learning evidence. A pupil unable to identify a trusted adult is supported privately, not pressed.

routes.Supported: Choose either task. Keep the flag words, bank, starter and visible model. Offer two action choices if needed. Point, type, use a usual aid or exact scribe with readback. Separate content cues from usual access.
routes.Independent: Choose either task. Identify each action, give reasons and suggest a respectful step and help route. Keep the model and usual aids. No real friendship account is needed.
routes.Aspire: Choose either task. Explain why one green action cannot cancel an amber concern. Consider a fair next step and what to do if it is not respected. Compare actions without labelling a person. No extra personal detail is required.

scaffolds.model: Accepting no shows respect for choice.
Accepting no is green because it respects a choice.
One kind act cannot prove the whole friendship is safe.
Choosing every step is amber because both need a say.
For the invented scene, a good friend can ask before sharing.

scaffolds.start: If the step is not respected…
scaffolds.model: The learner can ask trusted school staff for help.

hinge.question: One kind act happens, then a clear no is ignored. What should the learner judge?
choices: A The kind act means every action is safe.
B Judge each action and ask for help about the ignored no.
C Label the whole person with a colour.
D Keep quiet because friends must always agree.
hinge.parallel: A friend keeps choosing without asking. A Pause and seek a fair turn or trusted adult help. B Accept it because amber means harmless.
hinge.rule: Check privately. B or safe equivalent with a reason: proceed. A treats one act as proof; C labels a person; D removes choice. Re-model using the invented scene, then use parallel A. Pass or no response is unobserved; revisit with support, not a failure label.

timing: Settle, agree help and pause; choose a helpful action or give its reason.
Teach positive friendship, green and amber meanings; actions and context, not labels for people.
Model the invented scene; sort six behaviour cards with reasons or improve advice.
Check each action matters; choose map or note and usual response mode.
Scene map or advice note about the same invented scene; include optional private keep card.
Use shared checks; one next step and pupil response.
Explain a respectful step or repair a friendship myth. Confirm help.
where_this_leads: This helps me work with others, respect choices and ask for support in a group or future work.
marking: Retain actual fictional learning evidence, usual access and content prompts. Set one NS and allow a reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. E only for actual saved work. R only after Voice, Audience, one NS and an actual pupil response. Offer to the Communication portfolio; staff confirm any mapping. Personal keep cards and real concerns are not learning evidence. Any offer for the unit award depends on staff checking actual evidence and current requirements.

Identify features of positive friendships and relationships.
Use the invented scene. No real friend, relationship or private card is needed. Keep your usual aids. You can pass or ask for the agreed pause.
Make a two-part scene map. Identify one green and one amber action, give a reason for each, then suggest a respectful next step and help route. Work in your book. A map may be a list.

Write an advice note about the same scene. Explain one green and one amber action with reasons, then give a respectful next step and help route. Work in your book. Both choices use the same scene and checks.
Identify one green and one amber action in the invented scene. Give a reason for each. Suggest a respectful next step and a trusted adult help route. Judge actions in context, not a whole person.
Start: I judge this action… because…
Model: Choosing every step is amber because both need a say.

paragraphs: Identify features of positive friendships and relationships.

A positive friendship has care and respect. People can have different likes and other friends. They listen, ask before sharing and respect a no. One kind act does not prove that every part of a friendship is safe.

Green flag means this action shows care or respect. Amber flag means pause, check what happened and ask for help if needed. Judge the action and its context, not a whole person. Amber never means put up with harm. If someone feels unsafe, get a trusted adult at once; do not wait to finish a sort. These two labels are learning prompts, not a safety test.

Accept a reasoned safe interpretation that fits the stated action. Do not infer a whole person is safe from one green action. Card 5 ignores a clear no and needs adult support; do not treat amber as harmless.

Two invented young people plan a quiet craft task. One asks to use a drawing. The other says no. The first person accepts this and chooses a new idea. Later one keeps choosing each next step without asking. The other wants a fair turn to choose. No names, personal details or unkind words are shown.

Accepting no is a green flag because it respects choice. Choosing every step without asking is an amber flag because both people need a say. They could pause and agree a turn each, or ask school staff to help. Judge each action; one green action does not cancel the amber concern.
They could say, Can we each choose one step? If that is not respected, they can stop the task and ask trusted school staff in private.

Main B. A wrongly treats one kind act as proof. C labels the whole person. D removes choice. Re-model with the invented scene then use parallel A: pause for a fair turn or trusted adult help. A pass is unobserved. Check privately using the usual response mode.

Green means an action shows care or respect, not that every action is safe. Amber means pause, check and ask for support if needed; it never means put up with harm. A friendship allows different likes, other friends and a no. One positive action cannot cancel a concern.
